A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BRIGHT benchmark and provide readable main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices. Moved and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval evaluations, downstream QA experiments, reranking experiments, and continued-training and long-context analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical evaluations and adds precision/recall results and a Qwen retrieval condition for downstream theorem-based QA.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, reasoning-enhanced query generation, reranking procedures, and GritLM continued-training objectives are retained. The revised QA judging prompt changes evaluation rather than the retrieval method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 12 datasets and 1,384 queries, with unchanged dataset statistics in Table 1. The long-context and downstream QA tasks also remain; additional metrics and model conditions do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: The theorem-based downstream comparison expands from none/random/oracle contexts in v2 Table 48 to include Qwen retrieval in v4 Table 47. The main set of 13 retrieval models and the MiniLM, Gemini, and GPT-4 reranking comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 46 substantially revises the reported QA evaluation: five criteria covering accuracy, relevance, comprehensiveness, clarity, and objectivity are replaced by reference-content coverage with ten-point anchors and a REASON/SCORE format. v4 also adds Precision@10 and Recall@10 and removes the separate GPT-4 generation condition for StackExchange QA. These are evaluation changes, not evidence of improved performance under identical conditions.

E4.justification: The downstream document-source analysis adds actual Qwen retrieval for theorem-based QA, testing whether oracle-context benefits extend to an available retriever. The separate GPT-4 StackExchange QA replication disappears. The leakage-training, reranking, and long-context analyses remain.

E5.justification: The five-seed averaging and standard-deviation reporting for theorem-based QA are retained from v2 Table 48 in v4 Table 47, including the same practice for the added Qwen row. Annotation-agreement reporting and statistical-significance statements are unchanged; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: Many retrieval values change in Tables 2 and 34–39; for example, Qwen's Table 2 average changes from 24.3 to 22.5. Table 4 replaces closed-book/Qwen/oracle QA averages of 57.7/64.3/74.9 with 77.7/79.6/81.8 under revised grading. Precision/recall results and Qwen theorem-QA results are added, while the separate GPT-4 StackExchange QA results are removed.

T1.justification: The formal retrieval-task definitions and mathematical filtering criteria remain unchanged. Neither version adds original theorems or proofs; the new reasoning taxonomy is explanatory rather than a formal theoretical development.

C1.justification: v4 removes the abstract's quantified claim of over 6.6 points of QA improvement and the introduction's 6.6/17.2-point claims, retaining qualitative improvement claims. The central claims about benchmark novelty, retrieval difficulty, reasoning-enhanced queries, and resistance to document contamination remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix D categorizes the required reasoning as deductive, analogical, causal, or analytical and explains these categories through existing examples. This adds substantive interpretation of the benchmark's demands. The QA-evaluation caveats and limitations concerning subjective relevance and unaddressed modalities are retained.

D1.justification: v4 supplies direct GitHub code and Hugging Face dataset links and replaces the reproducibility section's Drive link with the project website. Hardware, model checkpoints, context limits, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged. Passage-splitting and false-negative guidance is relocated rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: New Appendix I expands the comparison with the already-cited RAR-b, distinguishing dataset construction, document characteristics, and practical objectives. The bibliography and broader related-work discussion remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds contents and acknowledgments, revises subsection titles and cross-references, relocates StackExchange construction guidance, and rewrites Section 5.2. Most prose and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 1 replaces its keyword-retrieval example, Figure 3 and Tables 3–4 change placement, and the QA prompt display expands. v4 removes the GPT-4 StackExchange QA table, adds two precision/recall tables, and extends the theorem-QA table with a Qwen row. The overall visual design remains similar.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful retrieval metrics, a practical Qwen QA comparison, and clearer reasoning and related-work explanations. However, it changes QA grading and removes the GPT-4 replication, while Table 46 substitutes {predicted_answer} for the problem. The PDFs do not establish whether this is a documentation error or an evaluation defect. Headline/table inconsistencies also persist: v2 states 22.1 against Table 2's 24.3, while v4 states 24.3 against 22.5. These tradeoffs prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
